rows.title: NFL wind: four Sunday totals to verify
rows.observation: The November 1 source selections are NE–MIA under 43.5 (-113), LAC–LAR under 45.5 (-111), ATL–TB under 43.5 (-111), and IND–JAX under 46.5 (-110). The screen uses average wind of at least 10 mph and temperatures from 33 to 90 degrees; displayed history is 635-467-10 with 11% ROI.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: these are source claims, not verified game-time weather effects. Stadium shelter and roof conditions can invalidate an outdoor weather proxy. Historical ROI is not a forecast for these four games.
rows.next_check: Verify venue, roof/open-air exposure and forecast near kickoff; compare the exact current total and price. Re-capture tomorrow before a new decision. No automatic wind adjustment.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: Portland–Utah: investigate the under
rows.observation: Action lists Under 232.5 at -112 as a system selection for October 31. Its displayed history is 534 wins, 434 losses, 9 pushes and 7% ROI. Filters include division games in the regular season, under support at 40% or less, and a total falling by at least one point from open to close.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: closing-line information is unavailable when an earlier ticket is placed. This is a third-party historical screen, not our calibrated win probability. The discovery row and expanded chart also disagree on total units; those units are not used.
rows.next_check: Compare the same sportsbook total at the actual decision time, verify line movement and current injuries/pace, then track an independent forward benchmark. Do not apply a fixed probability boost or copy the source stake.

rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.
rows.next_check: Keep source systems separate from agency results; test rules prospectively with timestamped inputs and realistic prices before changing betting behavior.

rows.title: College football: compare external model disagreements
rows.observation: At capture the dashboard displayed South Alabama +6.5 versus projection +2, Air Force +0.5 versus -3.5, and Kansas State +2.5 versus -1.2 for October 31 matchups. These are external model comparison leads, not accepted picks or verified book offers.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: a forecast disagreement identifies something to investigate. It does not establish which model is right. The dashboard supplies no named executable sportsbook for these displayed offers.
rows.next_check: Resolve full team/event identities and current sportsbook contracts, compare our forecast and injuries, and preserve the disagreement for later outcome scoring.

evidence_decisions.note: New paper evaluations use supported fresh evidence. CFBD quality-screen v1 is active for CFB moneylines and laying-points spreads: a joint offensive/defensive disadvantage with four-game samples raises required edge by 2 percentage points and caps stakes at one unit. It can change takes to passes without changing forecast probabilities. Totals and underdog spreads retain existing rules. Experimental, not proven profitable. Injury scenarios can change NBA prop forecasts (maximum 5 percentage points; half-unit stake cap). Falling minutes and matched moneyline crowding can raise required edge. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.
limitations: No unattended Action Network collection; snapshots expire after 30 minutes
Spread/total splits need exact source-line identity and remain display-only
Missing evidence retains the original forecast and is explicitly recorded
Existing tickets are never reselected or rewritten

decision_policy.note: Active experimental paper rule: for moneylines and spreads laying points (including pick-em), if the selected team has at least 0.05 lower offensive PPA/play AND at least 0.05 higher defensive PPA allowed than its opponent, require 2 additional percentage points of model edge and cap the stake at one unit. All four overall samples need at least four games and fresh, matched CFBD evidence. Totals, underdog spreads, missing/stale samples and mixed evidence retain existing rules. This is an unvalidated selection screen, not a calibrated probability model. Counterpoint keeps its inverse experiment.

claude_reviews.summary: Top observations (static review; no tests run, and the supplied test receipt is stale). (1) ai_budget.py:65 and 91 plus ai_research_worker.py:263-264: any single 'uncertain' row blocks ALL providers' paid calls indefinitely, and crashed 'reserved' rows are converted to uncertain at worker start with no reconciliation path in the supplied code. This is fail-closed (safe for money) but a likely availability lock-up; hypothesis that a reconcile tool exists elsewhere. (2) ai_budget.py:85 charges 2*inputs*rin while the reserve at line 51 is 2*((bytes+4096)*rin + out*rout), so the cost>reserved check at line 86 could raise on large token counts relative to bytes (tokens can exceed UTF-8 bytes rarely). On ValueError the reservation stays 'reserved' (rollback) and is later forced to 'uncertain' with the full reserve, and the provider call has already occurred. Definite edge risk, low probability. (3) ai_research_worker.py:158 counts Anthropic cache tokens at the uncached rate (conservative, fine), but line 59/60 retry eligibility and ai_budget.py:67 cooldown use started_utc string/time comparisons; retry bypasses cooldown only via recovery flag, and a 429 retry for OpenAI uses job_key 'retry:'+id, allowing one retry per prior id, so chains of retries on new rejected rows are possible within daily count limits (hypothesis). Also note ai_research_worker.py:112-113 hashes the review_key with week, so the weekly dedup works, but line 64-66 research evidence 'probability_adjustment' fields are passed to the reader, which is acceptable given the prompt forbids double boosts. No temporal leakage was found in the supplied excerpts; freshness windows are applied at lines 64, 70, 79 and 94.

Excerpts are truncated and I executed nothing; saved test evidence is for a different source snapshot, so none of this is validated. (1) nfl_props.py: acceptance is held (ACCEPTANCE_ENABLED=False, line 30), which is the right posture because probabilities come from a shifted-empirical-residual scenario (scenarios, lines 126-153) with no calibration check. Residuals are matched by position only, a single 2025 season pooled across players; mean+observed-prediction treats errors as homoscedastic and ignores player/volume scale, and pass-yds/rush-yds negative values are only clamped for counts. Pushes are excluded from the over probability but the edge at line 300 uses 1/decimal(price) against a no-push probability, which overstates edge on integer lines (push refunds, so EV differs). Bias is then added directly to probability (line 298-299) without calibration, risking miscalibration and a possible double adjustment with any agency/bankroll caps. (2) Settlement identity/accounting: nfl_props.settle (lines 239-271) updates the ticket, credits cash and inserts the settlement inside the caller's transaction only when tick holds it; settle passes through for ACCEPTANCE_ENABLED False, so hold mode still settles prior tickets, fine. Missing-stat zero/void logic (missing_stat_participation, lines 179-211) relies on roster status INA/RES for DNP, and a roster row is matched by week only; a status snapshot taken after the game could mislabel participation. This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed bug; needs data validation. (3) props_book.py: NBA result_for (lines 212-275) is reasonably defensive (points reconciliation, minute totals, duplicate rows), but tolerance of 0.5 min per active player plus 1 could admit incomplete data, and schedule status uses drop_duplicates(keep=False) silently marking games unverified. In tick (lines 382-383) belief and edge are computed, then immediately overwritten by context.prop probability; if the decision layer also applies group/private bias, bias is double-counted (props_book belief line 171-180 adds bias, then evidence context). Confirm the context.prop probability does not re-apply bias.

Top observations (hypotheses/missing validation unless noted; I did not run code): (1) sportsbook.py:106-109,133 plus evidence_decisions.py:92-94: the belief is a normal-error/fixed-bias heuristic and evidence blends or stake caps layer on top. The reported edge (sportsbook.py:189,191) is model probability minus implied price including vig, not calibrated EV, and the injury blend uses fixed WEIGHTS and a 5-point cap that are not validated; treat any promotion as unsupported. (2) Possible double adjustment: sportsbook.py:107-109 and 125 compute probability from owner markets, then context.game()/prop() adds evidence changes (evidence_decisions.py:134-135). The code uses a blend of the prior rather than an additive delta, which avoids stacking, but the CFB apply_policy (cfb_efficiency, not shown, called at evidence_decisions.py:166) cannot be verified for double adjustment from the supplied files. (3) Settlement/identity risks: sportsbook.py:82-90 matches by a 20-minute window and name/abbreviation set intersection, and the neutral-site reversal at 96-97 swaps home/away. Any mismatch directly misprices the ticket, though settlement in grade() (135-145) uses the stored side and appears sign-consistent. Also sportsbook.py:201 computes stake before the evidence cap, then 205 applies it only when set; bankroll accounting (cash deducted at 228, payout added at 172) looks consistent, but no test evidence applies since saved tests are for a different source snapshot. Rerun before approval. Temporal handling is mostly sound: quotes must precede tip and now (99), and evidence freshness is checked. evidence_decisions.py:122 uses a string date compare, which is fine for ISO dates.

bankroll_policy: New paper stakes: at most 40% committed overall, 10% per sport, 2% per game and 1% per ticket. At most 10% committed beyond 24 hours. Sportsbook NBA/NFL game lines may use 7.5% per sport, leaving 2.5% of bankroll for props within the 10% sport limit. Percentages use the lower of initial bankroll and current cash plus open stakes; profits do not automatically increase limits. Existing locked tickets remain intact, and may exceed new limits until settlement. Model and sportsbook accounts stay separate.
